Every knowledge statement for Vehicle emergencies, collision response and crash reporting is tied to one physical page of the registered Delaware handbook snapshot. No outside legal explanation or inferred exception is added.
Emergency maneuvers remain source-edition descriptions with their equipment and failure conditions; no action is described as guaranteeing a safe outcome. The shoulder-return speed is an upper-bound precondition, not a guarantee that re-entry at that speed is safe.
First-aid handling, firefighting, disputed skid/road-edge advice and broad airbag claims are withheld pending appropriate review. Reporting thresholds retain apparent damage, location and suspected-impairment qualifiers. Contact details remain dynamic, and the final notes pages supply no instructional facts.
Open source limitation (verify DE-EMERGENCY-EQUIPMENT): Parking-brake handle, wet-brake, ignition-lock and failed-brake instructions depend on vehicle equipment. Do not merge failed-brake pumping with normal ABS emergency braking or apply every mechanical step to every vehicle without manufacturer-specific verification.
Open source limitation (verify DE-EMERGENCY-ROAD-EDGE): The shoulder-return passage tells the driver to turn sharply after listed preconditions without describing edge drop, surface or vehicle constraints. That steering instruction is withheld pending technical safety review.
Open source limitation (verify DE-EMERGENCY-FIRE): The fire and crash passages describe self-extinguishing methods, a fixed separation distance and use of flares despite possible spilled fuel. These operational details are withheld pending current fire-safety guidance and site/equipment conditions.
Open source limitation (verify DE-EMERGENCY-RAIL): The stalled-track text suggests a restart attempt when no train is seen, but does not specify a full evacuation, emergency-notification or safe-restart procedure. The restart instruction is withheld pending applicable official rail-safety verification.
Open source limitation (verify DE-EMERGENCY-SKID): The generic skid-recovery passage does not distinguish skid type or ABS equipment and gives a blanket brake prohibition and repeated steering corrections. Those detailed recovery instructions are withheld pending technical review.
Open source limitation (verify DE-EMERGENCY-IMPACT): The impact-protection passage states that an airbag will inflate and gives collision-steering/bracing advice without deployment or crash-condition limits. These guarantees and specific impact maneuvers are withheld pending equipment and safety review.
Open source limitation (verify DE-EMERGENCY-FIRST-AID): The first-aid passage says not to move injured people except for specified immediate dangers, while a later aid duty includes transporting them for care. Medical handling, bleeding and shock directions are withheld pending qualified clinical/legal reconciliation.
Open source limitation (verify DE-EMERGENCY-REPORT-SCOPE): The own-property-only paragraph says immediately report without identifying its reporting channel or relation to the later threshold-based police-report list. That isolated obligation is withheld until its scope is clarified.
Open source limitation (verify DE-EMERGENCY-CONTACTS): Telephone numbers, service hours, email and web reporting availability are dynamic and have not been freshly verified. Agency identity and issue categories are supported; live contact details are not minted as stable facts.
Source quality: official issuer PDF. Extraction is text only; graphical content does not become a fact unless its supporting meaning is stated in the text. Unknown exam metadata and market evidence remain typed debt.
